newsitem.title: GREECE: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 18.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - GREEK FINANCIAL NEWS- AUG 18.

text.p: Leading stories in the Greek financial press:
IMERISIA
-- A minor cabinet reshuffle of deputy ministers is on the cards for early autumn. No changes are expected in economic ministries.
-- The prime minister is faced with tough and critical decisions on five areas of economic policy to be followed in 1998.

-- According to an internal report drafted by the National Bank, its strategy for raising its profits centers around the forthcoming capital increase, the acceleration of profitability in its subsidiaries and the sale of real estate holdings which has already contributed 7.0 billion drachmas.
EXPRESS

-- Economic policy will tighten in 1998 with inflation remaining its focal point. The guidelines for next year's economic policy will be articulated by the prime minister in his opening speach at the Thessaloniki trade fair in September 6.
SUNDAY ELEFTHEROTYPIA

-- The ministry of national economy plans to transfer European Union funds amounting to 920 billion drachmas included in the so-called 'Delhors II' financial aid package between sectors of the economy which present varying absorption rates. It is hoped that the completion of all co-funded infrastructure projects will be concluded by 1999, two years earlier than initially scheduled, in order to seek additional funding through a new financial aid package, dubbed the 'Santer package'.

-- The government is striving to bridge a 300 billion gap in its finances for 1997. Over the coming two months, it will step up its efforts in a bid to raise the rate of increase in fiscal revenues. Its prime target group will be tax-payers with payments in arrears in excess of 5.0 million drachmas. A black list of some 5,000 bad payers will be publicised in September.
SUNDAY VIMA

-- The government will be faced in the forthcoming autumn with the demanding task of meeting the targets of its economic policy and successfully carrying out the 1997 Budget and drafting the 1998 Budget.
SUNDAY KATHIMERINI

-- The development ministry's Monopolies' Commission is looking into pricing issues with Greece's two cellular telephone operators which are alleged to have struck a tacit agreement to eliminate price competition. OTE telecom is expected to enter the field of mobile telephony by year-end, undercutting rates by around 20 percent.

-- The ministry of agriculture is working towards setting a new payment schedule for social security contributions by the staff of agricultural co-operatives to their pension funds, estimated at 7.8 billion drachmas.
KATHIMERINI

-- OTE telecom, along with the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development, France Telecom and the Hellenic Bottling Company, has submitted a bid for the acquisition of a 90 percent stake in the Armenian telecom utility. OTE telecom is expcted to acquire a 51 percent stake and assume management of the Armenian company which is seen having very attractive growth prospects.

-- The so-called 'social dialogue' between the government, employers and labour force has come to a standstill over the past month or so, affected by the summer holiday season and the absence of a conciliatory spirit by the three parties.
KERDOS

-- The capital market is heating up by corporate moves within the National Bank group of companies. The bank is merging its subsidiaries operating in the fields of insurance and mortgage credit and is headed for a large capital increase around October.

-- The finance ministry is expected in September to revise upwards its set of objective prices used in the calculation of taxation for real estate transactions. --Angelos Kiosklis, Athens Newsroom +301 3311812-4
